@@ -1072,1 +1072,2 @@
-bool cas_membar_elidable(int opcode);
+bool cas_leading_membar_elidable(int opcode);
+bool cas_trailing_membar_elidable(int opcode);
@@ -1193,4 +1194,5 @@
-// Return true if the leading MemBarRelease and trailing MemBarAcquire around a
-// CAS-like LoadStore node may be elided, that is if the node is matched to a
-// single AMO instruction carrying both the aq and rl annotations:
-// amoswap/amoadd/amocas with .aqrl.
+// Return true if the trailing MemBarAcquire around a CAS-like LoadStore node
+// may be elided, that is if the node is matched to a single AMO instruction
+// carrying both the aq and rl annotations: amoswap/amoadd/amocas with .aqrl.
+// The leading MemBarRelease has a weaker condition of its own, see
+// cas_leading_membar_elidable() below.
@@ -1202,7 +1204,7 @@
-// An LR/SC based CAS is weaker. lr.aq + sc.rl only provides release-acquire,
-// not a sequentially consistent read-modify-write: the aq annotation sits on
-// the LR, so PPO rule 5 orders the *load* before later accesses, while the rl
-// annotation sits on the SC, so PPO rule 6 only orders earlier accesses before
-// the *store*. Nothing orders the SC's store before a subsequent load, so that
-// store may still be buffered when a load of an unrelated address is
-// satisfied.
+// An LR/SC based CAS has different ordering properties from a single AMO.
+// The aq annotation on LR orders its load before later accesses, while the
+// rl annotation on SC orders earlier accesses before its successful store.
+// These annotations must not be treated as .aqrl on a single instruction.
+// Without Zalasr, a subsequent volatile load uses a plain load followed by
+// fence r,rw, not an acquiring load carrying an RCsc annotation. PPO rule 7
+// therefore does not establish an SC-to-load edge for that plain load.
@@ -1210,15 +1212,3 @@
-// Emitting the membars does not supply that missing StoreLoad edge either,
-// since MemBarAcquire lowers to `fence r,rw`, whose predecessor set holds only
-// reads. Java code that needs the edge has to request it explicitly, and code
-// which fails to do so can lose a wakeup; see JDK-8387644. Elision is
-// nevertheless restricted here to the fully-ordered AMO forms, so that the
-// LR/SC path keeps the strength it had before the membars started being
-// elided. The leading MemBarRelease on its own would be safe to elide for
-// LR/SC too, since the rl annotation on the SC covers it by PPO rule 6, but
-// both are gated together to keep the two predicates symmetric.
-//
-// Whether the aq annotation is actually set is decided per node by
-// needs_acquiring_load_reserved(), which selects the *Acq instruct variants.
-// It holds for every opcode listed below on the paths reaching the two callers,
-// which assert as much.
-bool cas_membar_elidable(int opcode)
+// Keep the trailing MemBarAcquire for the existing LR/SC mapping rather than
+// extending the single-AMO elision to LR/SC.
+bool cas_trailing_membar_elidable(int opcode)
@@ -1251,5 +1241,1 @@
-    // Sub-word forms additionally require Zabha for amocas.{b|h}. Without it
-    // they are open coded around a narrow lr.w/sc.w or amocas.w, see
-    // cmpxchg_narrow_value(). The Zacas variant of that sequence can leave
-    // through its failure path having executed nothing but a plain lw, so it
-    // carries no ordering at all and its membars must be kept.
+    // Matched to amocas.{b|h}.aqrl only when Zacas and Zabha is available.
@@ -1268,0 +1254,52 @@
+// Return true if the leading MemBarRelease around a CAS-like LoadStore node may
+// be elided. The required release ordering places accesses preceding the CAS
+// before its successful store, and the rl annotation on that store provides
+// this ordering by PPO rule 6. This is the same release property relied on by
+// the is_Store() branch of unnecessary_release() for a releasing store.
+// An LR/SC pair therefore qualifies here, whereas cas_trailing_membar_elidable()
+// above restricts elision to a single AMO carrying both aq and rl annotations.
+bool cas_leading_membar_elidable(int opcode)
+{
+  assert(is_CAS(opcode, true), "expecting a compare and swap");
+
+  switch (opcode) {
+    // Matched to amoswap/amoadd.aqrl.
+    case Op_GetAndSetI:
+    case Op_GetAndSetL:
+    case Op_GetAndSetP:
+    case Op_GetAndSetN:
+    case Op_GetAndAddI:
+    case Op_GetAndAddL:
+      return true;
+    // Matched to amocas.{w|d}.aqrl with Zacas, to lr.{w|d}.aq + sc.{w|d}.rl
+    // without it. Both carry the rl annotation on their successful store.
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapI:
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapL:
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapP:
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapN:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeI:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeL:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeP:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeN:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapI:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapL:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapP:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapN:
+      return true;
+    // Sub-word forms reach amocas.{b|h}.aqrl with Zacas and Zabha. Otherwise
+    // they are open coded around lr.w/sc.w or amocas.w, with rl still set on
+    // the successful store. The Zacas expansion uses lw_acquire for its
+    // acquiring pre-check; early failure publishes no store, so it does not
+    // require a leading release fence either.
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapB:
+    case Op_CompareAndSwapS:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeB:
+    case Op_CompareAndExchangeS:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapB:
+    case Op_WeakCompareAndSwapS:
+      return true;
+    default:
+      return false;
+  }
+}
+
@@ -1281,1 +1319,1 @@
-    return cas_membar_elidable(load_store->Opcode());
+    return cas_trailing_membar_elidable(load_store->Opcode());
@@ -1321,1 +1359,1 @@
-      return cas_membar_elidable(mem->Opcode());
+      return cas_leading_membar_elidable(mem->Opcode());
